stem: Two fair dice are thrown simultaneously. Given that the sum of the two numbers is at least 9, what is the probability that the sum is exactly 11?

per_option_rationale.rationale: P(sum=11 | sum>=9) = n(sum=11 and sum>=9) / n(sum>=9) = 2/10 = 1/5. The 10 outcomes with sum>=9 are listed; exactly 2 give sum=11 ((5,6) and (6,5)).
Computing P(sum=11) over the full 36 outcomes: 2/36 = 1/18, ignoring the conditioning on sum>=9 and using the unreduced sample space.
Correctly finding 2 favourable outcomes and 10 in the restricted space but leaving the answer as 2/10 instead of simplifying to 1/5.
Counting only 12 outcomes for sum>=9 instead of the correct 10, giving 2/12 = 1/6.

explanation: The restricted sample space for sum>=9 has exactly 10 outcomes. Within that space, sum=11 corresponds to 2 outcomes: (5,6) and (6,5). P = 2/10 = 1/5.

explanation_sections.punchline: Conditional probability reduces the sample space to only those outcomes satisfying the given condition.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: conditional probability by restricted sample space. List sum>=9 outcomes: (3,6),(4,5),(4,6),(5,4),(5,5),(5,6),(6,3),(6,4),(6,5),(6,6) = 10 total. Of these, sum=11: (5,6),(6,5) = 2. P = 2/10 = 1/5.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always re-enumerate the restricted sample space rather than using the full 36 outcomes when a condition is given.
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. Systematically list sum>=9 outcomes row by row. The trap is forgetting the condition and dividing by 36 instead of 10.
